findings.title: Contradictory provider read envelopes can authorize submission or certify an observation
findings.rationale: api-app/src/integrations/meta/message-template.client.ts:225 accepts every HTTP-success JSON object in readObject. Unlike loadGrant and createTemplate, listTemplates and getTemplate do not reject an error envelope accompanying otherwise plausible data. Consequently HTTP 200 with error plus data:[] passes preflight as proven absence and permits POST; error plus a plausible APPROVED template can become an eligible observation. This violates D05's inconclusive-response prohibition and D07's requirement that provider errors preserve prior observations without fabricating an empty or successful result.
findings.suggested_action: A: Reject contradictory/error-bearing success wrappers in the shared read validator. B: Introduce strict operation-specific envelope validation for list and individual reads. C: Retain current permissiveness; this is unsuitable for absence or approval evidence. Recommend A with operation-specific shape checks retained. Verify contradictory preflight produces zero POSTs, and contradictory catalog/individual responses preserve prior content while marking it unavailable and ineligible.

findings.title: A completed correlation prevents the original ACK from improving the operation
findings.rationale: In api-app/src/domain/message-templates/template-submission.service.ts:564, recordOutcome updates only SENDING or AMBIGUOUS operations. If reconciliation commits CORRELATED_BY_DEFINITION first, a subsequent valid original ACK cannot update even an identical remote ID. Its readback also requires ACKNOWLEDGED provenance, so the request returns local-incomplete without retaining an ACK receipt, while persisted providerAcceptance remains UNKNOWN. D06 and CR-01 require monotonic enrichment of the same operation. The retained late-ACK test exercises ACK completion before the held recovery response, leaving the inverse ordering unprotected.
findings.suggested_action: A: Permit a captured original claim to atomically upgrade matching correlated acceptance to acknowledged acceptance and append its receipt. B: Retain confirmed original-ACK evidence separately when association cannot safely change, with explicit projection semantics and no silent rebinding. C: Leave current behavior; this cannot satisfy the frozen late-result contract. Recommend A for matching IDs and an explicit disposition for conflicting IDs. Verify both completion orders, matching and differing IDs, durable receipts, unchanged reservations and exactly one POST.

findings.title: The disclosed connector credential incident remains operationally unresolved
findings.rationale: evidence/executor-startup-secret-redaction-v1.1.json:4 records credential disclosure in rendered startup diagnostics, and its actions record artifact scrubbing and operator notification. The package explicitly states that rotation is unconfirmed and previously rendered output cannot be retracted. These mitigations do not establish credential invalidation. This is a residual operational security issue, not evidence that the template architecture or Meta credentials were compromised, and it must not be silently closed.
findings.suggested_action: A: Have the credential owner revoke/reissue it and record a secret-free confirmation. B: Obtain explicit security-owner acceptance with scope, owner and follow-up deadline if rotation cannot yet occur. C: Take no further action; retain the incident as unresolved. Recommend A. Verify disposition and continued exclusion of inherited connector configuration from reviewer startup without reproducing the secret or inspecting protected product paths. This finding does not require redesigning template management.

findings.title: Submission recovery can overwrite text edited while the request was pending
findings.rationale: web-app/src/telas/Modelos.tsx:454 and :482 use captured dirty values before replacing the form with authoritative.definition. enviar starts only when dirty is false, while editor fields remain writable until a later response locks the draft. If the seller edits during a held submission and its 503 recovery reads succeed, the old closure still executes setForm and erases those newer edits. Context/editor fences do not detect edits within the same editor. This contradicts D08's monotonic edit protection and the approved preservation of current text.
findings.suggested_action: A: Capture editEpoch at mutation start and check it before every later form replacement. B: Preserve the current form throughout recovery and adopt only durable identity, revision and savedDefinition. C: Leave the captured dirty check; this retains reproducible text loss. Recommend A, matching the existing save protection. Verify held submit followed by an edit and uncertain/local-incomplete recovery preserves the edited form, durable operation identity and no-replay behavior.

findings.title: Individual refresh completion loses the draft owner/admin authorization requirement
findings.rationale: TemplateObservationService.authorizeDraft initially checks ownership or ADMIN, but ownsLease at api-app/src/domain/message-templates/template-observation.service.ts:314 revalidates only an active actor, active BU and grant existence; its grant query selects userId without role. An administrator refreshing another seller's draft can therefore be downgraded to ATENDENTE during provider I/O and still commit and receive the individual result. The row locks preserve a grant that no longer authorizes that draft-specific operation. D01 and the frozen individual-refresh contract require owner/admin access.
findings.suggested_action: A: Recheck the captured draft's ownership and current BU role inside the completion transaction. B: Pass a producer-specific authorization predicate into the shared lease completion path, retaining ATENDENTE access for catalog refresh. C: Keep existence-only revalidation; this leaves the authorization exception unresolved. Recommend A or B without raising catalog permissions. Verify a held individual response after ADMIN-to-ATENDENTE downgrade cannot write or disclose the draft-specific result; retain positive owner and catalog cases.

findings.title: Failed individual refresh leaves previously approved UI copies eligible
findings.rationale: At web-app/src/telas/Modelos.tsx:519, atualizarStatus handles failure by setting an error only. The backend marks the shared observation unavailable and observedEligible=false, but the browser retains its prior APPROVED individualStatus and catalog copies with available=true. Unlike catalog refresh failure, this path does not set a blocking availability flag or reload the persisted observation. The screen can continue displaying eligibility until TTL expiry despite a known current refresh failure, contrary to D07.
findings.suggested_action: A: Under the current UI fence, preserve prior content but invalidate availability and eligibility across its individual and catalog copies. B: Read back the shared persisted observation through an observational endpoint, keeping eligibility disabled until confirmed. C: Preserve the present eligible display; this violates the error-state contract. Recommend A, optionally followed by B. Verify APPROVED followed by individual timeout/malformed response immediately becomes unavailable and ineligible, and that an older error cannot invalidate a newer success.

findings.title: Draft and operation GETs omit the shared persisted observation
findings.rationale: TemplateDraftService.projectWithOperations returns draft/operation/receipt data at api-app/src/domain/message-templates/template-draft.service.ts:255, and TemplateSubmissionService.projectOperation at :663 likewise omits observations. Opening a draft clears individualStatus in Modelos.tsx:302. Thus an individual PAUSED observation obtained before any catalog page exists cannot be recovered after reload without another provider refresh. D07, the operation GET contract and CR-V11-01 explicitly require draft/catalog/GET/reload projections to derive from the same observation. The browser reload scenario refreshes remotely before asserting individual PAUSED, so its pass does not close this gap.
findings.suggested_action: A: Reuse the observation owner's bounded read projector in draft/operation DTOs and restore that state when opening the draft. B: Seek renewed approval for reduced GET/reload semantics; no such exception currently exists. C: Leave the omission and keep this contract unmet. Recommend A without provider calls or writes in GET. Verify individual PAUSED with no catalog page survives draft GET, operation GET and browser reload; also verify TTL, changed-context ineligibility and both producer directions.
